speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you've had a fever and changes in your mental state for two days. To help me understand what's going on, have you experienced any severe headaches, stiff neck, seizures, or confusion?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

I have noted your age, the two-day fever with altered mental status, and importantly, your history of tics and current use of haloperidol. Given the absence of headache, neck stiffness, or seizures, and the presence of fever and altered mentation while on an antipsychotic, NMS is the leading clinical suspicion. I am requesting the following: REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CMP (specifically Creatine Kinase), and Coagulation Profile. Please also provide the latest vital signs, specifically blood pressure and temperature, and any available images of your physical exam.
